note: Grade 3 addsub builds 12 stacked addition and subtraction problems with 3-digit numbers, sums kept within 1000, any method fits the work space; the estimate check is not printed, the teacher can ask for it.

Grade 3 compare makes pairs with the same numerator or the same denominator, each drawn as two equal bars to shade and compare with <, > or =; count l gives 10 pairs (closest to 12); the written reason is not prompted but the bars are the reason.
Grade 3 compo draws 6 L-shaped figures with all six sides labeled and asks for the area; the key and teacher page show the split-into-rectangles or big-minus-small working.
Grade 4 addsub stacks 12 problems with 4- and 5-digit numbers in standard-algorithm layout; regroup=with makes every problem regroup, though regrouping across zeros is not guaranteed on every sheet.
Grade 4 mul gives 12 stacked problems (2-digit by 2-digit and up to 4-digit by 1-digit) with space to write partial products; the estimate check on 3 of them is not printed.

Grade 4 div gives 12 long-division bracket problems, 3- and 4-digit dividends by 1-digit divisors with remainders written as R; partial quotients fit the bracket layout, drawings are the student's own.
Grade 4 mixed adds and subtracts mixed numbers with like denominators, 12 problems (closest to 10), answers in simplest mixed form and worked steps on the teacher page including regrouping a whole.
Grade 4 missing gives 9 text problems (closest to 8): a rectangle with a given area or perimeter and one side, find the other side; key shows the working.
Grade 5 mul stacks 12 problems of 3-digit by 2-digit numbers for the standard algorithm; the estimate check is not printed.
Grade 5 div gives 12 long-division problems, 4-digit dividends by 2-digit divisors (11 to 49), remainders as R; the bracket layout takes partial quotients, area models are the student's own.
Grade 5 addunlike adds and subtracts fractions with unlike denominators (LCD at most 60), 12 problems, steps on the teacher page show the renaming; about 3 in 10 involve a mixed number.
Grade 5 volc draws 6 solids made of two joined boxes (an L in front view) with all dimensions labeled; the key adds the two prism volumes.
Grade 7 ineq2 gives 8 two-step inequalities with a blank number line under each; coefficients range over negatives so some flip the sign, and the key graphs each answer.
Grade 8 dist gives 8 equations of the form p(x + q) = r that need the distributive property, with integer (so rational) coefficients and stepwise solutions on the teacher page.
Crossword built from the Life Cycles Word Wall with meanings as clues; 10 words (the largest count) instead of 12, and the order-a-scrambled-cycle extra is not made.
Grade 3 claim-evidence-reasoning frame (question, claim, two evidence boxes, reasoning, conclusion) with the meerkat question as the printed prompt.
Grade 4 claim-evidence-reasoning frame with the cactus prompt printed; students supply the two structures as evidence.
Grade 3-5 science observation log: prediction line plus four dated observation boxes with a drawing space, one per week, and two reflection prompts.
Grade 5 claim-evidence-reasoning frame with the sun-brightness question as the printed prompt.
Single-trait complete-dominance crosses with real traits; students fill each square and give genotype and phenotype ratios plus one probability. Four crosses per sheet (the largest count), not eight.
Two-circle Venn labeled Sexual and Asexual with a sum-it-up box; students add their own organism examples in the circles.

Grade 9-12 science log: hypothesis, independent, dependent and controlled variable boxes, a trial data table, sketch or graph space and a sources-of-error box; the student names the one variable tested.
Grade 9 claim-evidence-reasoning frame with alternate explanation, rebuttal and limitations; the topic prompt asks for the feedback and its evidence.
Grade 9 claim-evidence-reasoning frame with the pocket mouse prompt; variation, inheritance, selection and time go in the reasoning section.

Grade 3 map-skills draws one map with a lettered-and-numbered grid, a compass rose with NE/SE/SW/NW, a key and a scale bar (1 square = 100 m), then asks about 8 questions that use all four: what is in a square, which square a place is in, cardinal and intermediate directions, a scale distance, a route and a draw-a-star. Only gap: the map is a made-up town, not a state map, and the row says 10 questions.

Grade 8 argument frame (2-page drafting space) with the claim printed as the topic: introduction with claim, Body 1 and Body 2 reason-evidence-explanation, Body 3 opposing claim answered with evidence, conclusion, plus a linking-word bank and a standards checklist. Gap: two evidence bodies instead of three, and the sheet does not reference the corkboard from row 35.
